- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price drop is steep.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to ignore downward momentum; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for 7–10 days.
